style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The Venite -- 'O come' -- the psalm the Western church has sung at the opening of its daily office since at least the sixth century, when Benedict's Rule set it at the head of the night vigil, and at Morning Prayer since Cranmer's Prayer Book -- and the psalm the letter to the Hebrews spends two chapters expounding. It has two halves that seem not to belong together until you see that they do. The first is pure summons: come, sing, shout to the Rock of our salvation; He holds the earth's unexplored depths and the mountain peaks, He made the sea and shaped the land -- so come lower now, bow, kneel before our Maker, for we are His pasture-people, the flock His hand tends. Then, mid-verse, the Shepherd's own voice breaks in, and the invitation becomes a warning: today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts as at Meribah and Massah, where a generation that had watched the Red Sea part still put God on trial -- and the loathing of forty years stood under an oath sworn at Kadesh: they shall not enter My rest. Worship and warning are one psalm because the same voice speaks both; the flock that will not hear today has already begun to wander. Hebrews takes the 'today' and keeps it open: there remains a rest for the people of God, and the door is the one word -- hear.

1.text: Come, let us sing out with ringing joy to the LORD; let us raise a shout to the Rock of our salvation!
1.amp: O come [yalak], let us sing [ranan -- ring out with joy] unto the LORD [YHWH]: let us make a joyful noise [rua -- raise a shout] to the rock [tsur] of our salvation [yesha].
1.notes: The Venite, the church's invitatory psalm for some fifteen centuries. Two noise-verbs: ranan (H7442), the ringing cry, and rua (H7321), the war-shout that brought Jericho down -- worship loud enough to be heard outside the sanctuary, aimed at tsur yishenu (H6697, H3468), the Rock who saves.

2.text: Let us come to meet His face with thanksgiving; let us raise a shout to Him with songs of praise.
2.amp: Let us come before ['prevent his face', qadam panim, the KJV margin -- come to meet] His presence with thanksgiving [todah], and make a joyful noise [rua] unto Him with psalms [zemirot -- songs].
2.notes: qadam (H6923) is to go out ahead and meet -- the KJV's old 'prevent' -- so worship is pictured as running to intercept God's panim (H6440) with todah (H8426), the thank-offering's own word, in hand.

3.text: For the LORD is a great God, and a great King over all gods.
3.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] is a great [gadol] God [El], and a great King [melek] above all gods [elohim].
3.notes: El gadol and melek gadol (H410, H1419, H4428) -- greatness in nature and in office. 'Above all elohim' (H430) concedes nothing to the rival gods' reality; it ranks them below the One who made the deeps they were supposed to rule.

4.text: In His hand are the unexplored depths of the earth, and the peaks of the mountains are His as well.
4.amp: In His hand [yad] are the deep places [mechqar -- the unsearched depths] of the earth [eretz]: the strength ['the heights of the hills are his', toaphah, the KJV margin] of the hills [har] is His also.
4.notes: mechqar (H4278), from the root 'to search out': the earth's unexplored places, held in one yad (H3027). Depths and toaphot harim (H8443, H2022), the mountain peaks -- the vertical extremes of creation, both in the same grip.

5.text: The sea is His, for He made it, and His hands shaped the dry land.
5.amp: The sea [yam] is His, and He made [asah] it: and His hands [yad] formed [yatsar -- shaped like a potter] the dry [yabbesheth] land.
5.notes: asah and yatsar (H6213, H3335): the general making-verb, and the potter's shaping-verb Genesis 2:7 uses for the forming of man, applied to the yam and the yabbesheth (H3220, H3006) -- the two halves of creation's third day. Ownership by authorship.

6.text: Come, let us bow in worship and bend low; let us kneel before the LORD who made us.
6.amp: O come [bo], let us worship [shachah -- prostrate ourselves] and bow down [kara -- bend the knee]: let us kneel [barak] before [panim] the LORD [YHWH] our maker [asah].
6.notes: The second 'come', and the posture drops: from shouting (v. 1) to shachah, kara, barak (H7812, H3766, H1288) -- prostrate, bent, kneeling. barak here shares its letters with the Hebrew for 'knee'; the older lexicons took blessing to be, at root, going down on the knees, and whether or not the two are one root, the psalm puts them side by side: to bless God is to kneel before the One who asah (H6213) us.

7.text: For He is our God, and we are the people of His pasture, the flock His hand tends. Today, if only you would hear His voice --
7.amp: For He is our God [Elohim]; and we are the people [am] of His pasture [mirith], and the sheep [tson] of His hand [yad]. To day [yom] if ye will hear [shama] His voice [qol],
7.notes: The psalm's hinge, mid-verse: praise turns to warning. am marito and tson yado (H5971, H4830, H6629, H3027) -- pasture-people, hand-flock -- and then hayom (H3117), TODAY, the word Hebrews 3-4 presses for two whole chapters: as long as it is called today, shama (H8085) His qol (H6963).

8.text: do not let your hearts grow stiff, as at Meribah, as on that day of testing at Massah in the wilderness,
8.amp: Harden [qashah -- stiffen] not your heart [lebab], as in the provocation ['contention', Meribah, the KJV margin], and as in the day [yom] of temptation [Massah -- testing] in the wilderness [midbar]:
8.notes: qashah lebab (H7185, H3824), the stiffened heart of Pharaoh, now warned against in God's own people. Meribah and Massah (H4808, H4531) are place-names made of verbs -- Quarrel and Test -- from the water-crisis of Exodus 17: the day Israel put God on trial in the midbar (H4057).

9.text: when your fathers put Me to the test; they tried Me, though they had seen My work.
9.amp: When your fathers [ab] tempted [nasah -- tested] Me, proved [bachan -- assayed] Me, and saw [raah] My work [poal].
9.notes: nasah and bachan (H5254, H974): the testing-verbs God is entitled to use on men, here turned by men on God -- and 'though they raah My poal (H7200, H6467)': the test was conducted by eyewitnesses of the Red Sea. Unbelief is not usually a shortage of evidence.

10.text: For forty years I loathed that generation, and I said, 'They are a people whose hearts wander astray, and they have not known My ways.'
10.amp: Forty [arbaim] years [shanah] long was I grieved [qut -- loathed, was disgusted] with this generation [dor], and said [amar], It is a people [am] that do err [taah -- wander, stray] in their heart [lebab], and they have not known [yada] My ways [derek]:
10.notes: qut (H6962) is visceral disgust, forty years of it -- a whole dor (H1755) that taah (H8582), strayed like sheep, in the lebab, and never yada (H3045) His derek (H1870). The fault was not geography but the heart; they wandered inwardly first.

11.text: So I swore in My anger, 'They shall never enter into My rest.'
11.amp: Unto whom I sware [shaba] in My wrath [aph] that they should not enter ['if they enter into my rest', the KJV margin -- a Hebrew oath-formula] into My rest [menuchah].
11.notes: shaba be-aph (H7650, H639): an oath in anger, and the Hebrew's broken-off 'if they enter...' (the self-curse left unspoken) that the KJV margin preserves. menuchah (H4496), the rest -- Canaan for that generation, and per Hebrews 4:9 a sabbath-rest still open, which is why the psalm's 'today' is still being sung.
